name: Summer savory

schedule.notes: Surface-sow; needs light. Doesn't love transplanting.
Cut whole stems just before flowering. Plant grows back for a second cut.

harvest.cues: Stems 6 to 8 in, buds tight. Strip leaves with thumb and forefinger.
harvest.storageNotes: Dries excellently. Flavor concentrates — use sparingly dried.

varieties.name: Summer Savory
varieties.notes: The classic bean herb — pepper-thyme flavor. Plant alongside beans, beetles seem to dislike it.

notes: Called the 'bean herb' for good reason: pairs perfectly with green beans, dried beans, lentils. Cousin Winter Savory is a hardy perennial with stronger flavor.
